transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. What brings you to see me today?

Hi. Well, what made me come in today is that I've been having a hard time focusing lately. I work as a receptionist, and I've started losing my place while I’m scheduling appointments, or even when I'm just working on the lobby displays. 

It's like... my mind just slips off track. I get so busy thinking about what I might have overlooked or forgotten, and I just lose my train of thought completely. It's starting to get frustrating, so I figured I should talk to someone about it.
Besides work, do you find yourself constantly worrying about a lot of different everyday things in your life?

Yeah, I do. It's... I find myself worrying about all kinds of ordinary things now. Not just the big stuff, but everyday things like bills, travel plans, work schedules... even just little paperwork errors. I get this feeling like one small mix-up is going to somehow turn into a much bigger problem.
Do you find it difficult to control or stop these worries once they start?

Yeah, I really do. I try to stop it... I can even tell myself, 'Sunny, it’s handled,' but the thought just keeps looping anyway. It's like I can't just turn it off. And pretty soon I’ve gone from that one concern to another, until I’m just checking and rechecking details in my head over and over.
About how long have you been dealing with this kind of constant worrying?

Well, it's been going on for about nine months now. It all really started after... well, I had this overnight detention, and there was a big paperwork mix-up with it. Ever since then, the worrying just hasn't stopped.
Over these past several months, have you also been feeling down, depressed, or sad?
No, not really. I mean, I'm stressed and anxious, obviously, but I wouldn't say I feel depressed or sad. It's more just the constant worrying that's getting to me.
Do you feel driven to perform certain repetitive physical actions or routines, such as repeatedly checking locks, reorganizing items, or re-reading things over and over, to help relieve your anxiety?

No, I don't really do anything like that. Like I said, I'll go over things in my head a lot, just checking the details mentally, but I don't physically have to go check locks or reorganize my desk or anything. It's all just up in my head.
Along with this worrying, have you noticed physical symptoms like feeling restless, keyed up, or having tense muscles?

Yeah, I have. Um, especially at work. Like, at the front desk I can still smile and help people, but inside I just feel wound really tight. It's almost like my shoulders are constantly up around my ears, and I’m just... waiting for something to go wrong.

final_diagnosis.reason: The patient exhibits persistent, excessive, and generalized anxiety and worry across multiple everyday domains (work, bills, travel, paperwork) that is difficult to control. Associated symptoms include concentration difficulties/mind going blank, feeling keyed up/wound tight, and notable muscle tension, with symptoms persisting for approximately nine months and causing work-related impairment. Depressive symptoms and compulsive rituals are denied.
